title: SDK Retry Sherpa: token-aware backoff defaults and dedup-key contract for partial/streaming responses
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: SDK users frequently hit transient network or infra errors when calling generation and streaming endpoints. Existing retry guidance is fragmented across languages and is not token-aware, which causes either wasted compute (aggressive retries for long responses) or poor availability (too conservative for short requests). We also lack a consistent runtime contract for deduplication / idempotency keys when streaming partial responses back to callers. This ticket defines a cross-SDK default policy (the 'Sherpa' defaults) that is token-budget-aware, defines dedup-key semantics for partial/streamed responses, and provides concrete examples for Python/TS/Go clients.
goals: Create a single, opinionated default RetryPolicy that is safe for most production workloads and can be overridden per-request
Define a deduplication key contract that covers full-response and partial/streamed responses (including chunk-level resume semantics)
Provide language examples for setting policies and keys (Python / TypeScript / Go) and add unit/integration tests
Add telemetry hooks (retry_count, backoff_ms, dedup_hit, resume_attempt) and docs for SRE/PM visibility
non_goals: Force every customer to use Sherpa defaults (customers may supply custom RetryPolicy or disable retries)
Change server-side semantics beyond agreed compatibility (this is client-side behavior + doc contract)
constraints: Keep defaults conservative for large-token requests to avoid duplicate billing and wasted model compute
Backoff algorithm must be implementable consistently across Python/TS/Go and compatible with existing retry instrumentation
proposed_solution: Overview: Introduce 'SherpaRetryPolicy' in each SDK with the following properties: 1) token-aware initial timeout and max attempts 2) adaptive backoff multiplier derived from estimated remaining tokens 3) separate streaming resume policy with chunk checksums and resume window. Dedup-key contract: clients must send a deduplication key header (X-Redwood-Dedupe-Key) or param for non-streaming and streaming requests. For streaming, the client-provided dedupe key ties the entire request + subsequent resume attempts to one logical output. Server will maintain a short-lived ledger (server TTL) of completed responses and partial-chunk fingerprints. Clients that re-open a stream must provide a last-received-chunk-sequence and chunk-checksum; server will either resume from next chunk or instruct client to restart, depending on ledger state. Defaults: - Max attempts: min(5, 1 + floor(token_estimate/1024)) - Initial backoff: 200ms for token_estimate <=512, 500ms for 513-2048, 1000ms for >2048 - Backoff multiplier: 1.6 (exponential) with jitter +-20% - Max backoff cap: 30s - Token-aware budget: per-request retry budget limits cumulative re-generated tokens to <= 25% of original token_estimate (unless caller overrides). Streaming resume: - Resume window: server maintains chunk fingerprints for last 60s or 5MB of output, whichever comes first - Resume attempts allowed: up to 2 automatic resume attempts before surfacing failure - Partial response dedup semantics: on retry, server will avoid re-emitting chunks already confirmed by the client (checksum matches). Implementation notes: SDKs expose a RetryPolicy object and a convenience SherpaRetryPolicy() factory. SDKs must surface telemetry hooks and a high-level console-friendly log line for each retry/resume attempt.
examples:
Python example:
from redwood import Client, SherpaRetryPolicy
client = Client(api_key=..., retry_policy=SherpaRetryPolicy())
# Non-streaming with explicit dedupe key
resp = client.generate(prompt, dedupe_key="order-123-payflow")

# Streaming with resume metadata
stream = client.stream_chat(messages, dedupe_key="chat-abc-42")
for chunk in stream:
    process(chunk)
# on network fail: client will attempt resume with last_seq and last_checksum

Go example:
cli, _ := redwood.NewClient(redwood.Config{APIKey: os.Getenv('RW_KEY'), RetryPolicy: redwood.SherpaRetryPolicy()})
resp, err := cli.Generate(context.Background(), redwood.GenerateParams{Prompt: prompt, DedupeKey: 'txn-555'})
// Stream resume: client.StreamChat(ctx, params) returns a stream object with Resume(seq, checksum)
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs implement SherpaRetryPolicy with matching defaults and unit tests
Crosslang integration test that simulates network drop mid-stream and validates resume attempt behavior
Docs page and quickstart snippets for dedupe header/param usage
Telemetry emitted for retry_count, backoff_ms, dedup_hit, resume_attempt and surfaced in Console as new chart
Security review for header usage and privacy of dedupe keys completed
comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Chen: Drafted initial policy. Focused on token-budget and streaming resume to avoid duplicate model compute. Needs API ergonomics review from SDK leads.

2026-03-02 - Miguel Torres: Reviewed Python/TS ergonomics. Suggest exposing an opt-in 'aggressive_mode' override for low-latency interactive apps; flagged potential billing implications for aggressive retries.
2026-03-05 - SRE (Priya Rao): Asked for telemetry event shapes and suggested including 'original_token_estimate' and cumulative_retry_tokens to SLO dashboards.
2026-03-08 - Legal (Samir Patel): Requested guidance in docs about customer responsibility for dedupe key content (avoid PII in dedupe keys).
2026-03-10 - Miguel Torres: Implemented PoC in TypeScript; found corner case when client provides wrong last_checksum — server should prompt full restart rather than blind resume.
